- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (e.g., 2022-11-21, 2022-11-22).
- Forecasts show a gradual upward trend that doesn’t match the true outcome’s volatility or sharp corrections.
- After a spike in price (e.g., 80+), model tends to overshoot and then slowly decay — but doesn’t capture the immediate correction or mean reversion.
- Model fails to account for sudden drops or “reset” events (e.g., 82.26 → 77.50, 85.32 → 79.03) — underestimates downside risk.
- Forecasts are too smooth; lack of noise or volatility clustering in true outcomes.
- Model exhibits “lag” — forecasts are often 1–2 days ahead of actual price movements, especially in downward trends.
- Model overfits to recent high prices, ignoring historical mean or seasonal patterns.
- When true price drops sharply after a peak, model doesn’t adjust downward quickly — continues to trend upward.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of corrections after spikes — e.g., 88.93 → 86.19, model still rising.
- Model doesn’t capture “reversion to mean” after sustained high prices — tends to hold high forecasts even when prices fall.
